name: rlm
description: Recursive Language Model (RLM). Delegates a text-processing task to a sub-agent that recursively chunks large input and merges results (arxiv:2512.24601). WHEN TO USE: call this when you need to summarize, analyze, extract from, or transform a piece of text that is too long to handle in a single pass — the sub-agent splits it into manageable parts, processes each, and merges them. Also useful for any heavy text transformation (e.g. rewrite, translate, classify) on long documents. WHEN NOT TO USE: (1) do NOT use this for short texts you can process directly in your reply; (2) do NOT use this to review your own past reasoning traces — use the 'reasoning' tool for that instead. INPUT: {'instruction': required string describing what to do (e.g. 'summarize', 'extract all error codes', 'rewrite as bullet points'), 'text': required string containing the full text to process, 'depth': optional integer (internal recursion counter, defaults to 0; callers should omit this)}.
llm_description: Delegate a text task to a sub-agent that recursively chunks large input and merges results. Use for summarize/analyze/extract/transform on text too long for one pass; skip for short text or for reviewing your own reasoning traces (use 'reasoning'). Input: {instruction, text, depth?} (depth is internal, omit it).
